description: Works to trees covered by LBE ORDER NO 15 (4) 1971: PROPOSAL A - 1x Holly (T3) crown lift to 3m above ground level, retain shrub below. PROPOSAL B - 1x Yew (T1) - crown lift to 2.4m above ground level, reduce lateral growth from boundary wall by up to 2m, shape remainder, 1x Holly (T3) - crown reduce by up to 2m, cutting back to a side branch and leaving a flowing branch line without stumps, 1x Ash (T4) - crown lift to 3m above ground level, retain lower secondary stem, crown reduce by up to 3m cutting back to a side branch and leaving a flowing branch line without stumps, shorten lateral growth and shape by 2m, remove deadwood.

application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
decision_conditions: This consent is valid for two years.Reason: In order that the nature of work pertaining to this consent remains appropriate.

The works hereby approved shall only be carried out strictly in accordance with British Standard 3998 [2010] 'Tree Works'.Reason: In the interests of the health, safety and appearance of the preserved tree.

Tree work should not be carried out during periods that are likely to interfere with or disturb breeding birds or mammals.Reason: In order to comply with the requirements of the Wildlife and Countryside Act (1981) and Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations (2010).

The proposed crown reduction works to T1 and T3 would have a negative impact upon the tree's long-term health, and the tree's amenity value. In the absence of sufficient supporting evidence to demonstrate the necessity of the proposals, the stated reasons for the work are considered unjustified.

The proposed crown reduction works to T4 would have a significantly negative impact upon the tree's long-term health, and the tree's amenity value. The reasons for the proposal appear to be due to concerns over the tree's structural condition, yet the application form has "No" selected, when asked if the reasons for carrying out the proposed works are due to the condition of the tree. The application therefore is not consistent and contradicts itself. The proposed crown lifting of T4 is considered more than necessary.
The proposed crown lifting and lateral pruning of T1 to create clearances between the ground and built structures is considered not applicable due to those desired clearances already being present.
